# Flowtinus

> Visual data flows: components connected by edges move envelopes (each with a DATA object) from a Start to an End. A remote MCP server (/mcp on the API) lets an agent list components, read and write flow drafts, validate them and test run them.

## Docs

- [The flow file](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/flow-format.md): the YAML an agent writes, ports, expressions, rules, patterns (barrier, incremental load with a checkpoint, lock), a full example
- [Components](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/README.md): every component, by palette section
- [Connection types](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/connections.md): the profiles components connect with
- [MCP server](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/mcp/README.md): tools, scopes, personal access tokens, client setup
- [Runtime](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/runtime/README.md): supervisors, workers, who runs what

## Components

- [MongoDB Delete](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/mongodb-delete.md) (`mongodb-delete`): For each envelope, deletes every document of the collection (database and collection fixed or expressions on the envelope) that matches the filter (an expression on the envelope, as in mongosh) and the envelope goes on with {deleted} in its output key (default `mongodb`).
- [MongoDB Pipeline](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/mongodb-pipeline.md) (`mongodb-pipeline`): Runs an aggregation pipeline (written as in Compass or mongosh, an expression on the incoming envelope: `{$match: {cpf: $cpf}}`) on a collection (database and collection fixed or expressions on the envelope) once per incoming envelope and yields one envelope per document, the fields written into DATA.
- [MongoDB Upsert](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/mongodb-upsert.md) (`mongodb-upsert`): Writes each envelope into a collection (database and collection fixed or expressions on the envelope; batches kept per collection): updates ($set) or replaces the document matching the filter, or inserts it.
- [Redshift Delete](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/redshift-delete.md) (`redshift-delete`): Deletes the rows of an Amazon Redshift table whose Match on columns all equal the envelope's values (each a value or an expression on the envelope; null or undefined is an error for that envelope, never a wider delete).
- [Redshift Execute](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/redshift-execute.md) (`redshift-execute`): Runs any SQL on Amazon Redshift (one or more statements; nothing checks what it does) once per envelope, in a transaction of its own: a COMMIT or ROLLBACK in the SQL is its own; what is still open at the end is committed (At the end: Commit, the default) or rolled back; an error rolls back.
- [Redshift Insert](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/redshift-insert.md) (`redshift-insert`): Inserts one row per envelope into an Amazon Redshift table, each column a value or an expression on the envelope.
- [Redshift Query](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/redshift.md) (`redshift`): Runs a read-only query (one SELECT or WITH) on Amazon Redshift once per incoming envelope and yields one envelope per row, the columns written into DATA (Override: only the columns).
- [Redshift Upsert](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/redshift-upsert.md) (`redshift-upsert`): Writes one row per envelope into an Amazon Redshift table: the row whose Match on columns are equal is updated, otherwise it is inserted (Redshift does not enforce primary keys).
- [SQL Server Delete](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/sqlserver-delete.md) (`sqlserver-delete`): Deletes SQL Server rows, one DELETE per envelope: the rows whose Match on columns all equal the envelope's values (each a value or an expression on the envelope; null or undefined is an error for that envelope, never a wider delete).
- [SQL Server Execute](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/sqlserver-execute.md) (`sqlserver-execute`): Runs any SQL on SQL Server (one or more statements; nothing checks what it does) once per envelope, in a transaction of its own: a COMMIT or ROLLBACK in the SQL is its own; what is still open at the end is committed (At the end: Commit, the default) or rolled back; an error rolls back.
- [SQL Server Insert](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/sqlserver-insert.md) (`sqlserver-insert`): Inserts one row per envelope into a SQL Server table, each column a value or an expression on the envelope (an identity or defaulted column can be left out).
- [SQL Server Query](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/sqlserver.md) (`sqlserver`): Runs a read-only query (one SELECT or WITH) once per incoming envelope and yields one envelope per row, the columns written into DATA (Override: only the columns).
- [SQL Server Update](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/sqlserver-update.md) (`sqlserver-update`): Updates SQL Server rows, one UPDATE per envelope: the rows whose Match on columns equal the envelope's values get the other columns (each a value or an expression on the envelope).
- [HTTP Request](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/http-request.md) (`http-request`): Sends one request per envelope (method, URL, query params, headers and body are values or expressions on it; $SECRETS works; the body as it is, or a multipart form of fields and text files) and the envelope goes on with {status, headers, body} in its output key (default `response`; a JSON body parsed).
- [Script Invoker](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/script.md) (`script`): Calls, for each envelope, a function a project script exports (`path#name`), its arguments in the order of its parameters, each a value or an expression on the envelope.
- [TypeScript](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/typescript.md) (`typescript`): Runs `async function process($input)` for each envelope ($input is its DATA).
- [Aggregate](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/aggregate.md) (`aggregate`): Groups the envelopes into batches of N, or All of them in one batch when the input ends, and yields one envelope per batch with the list of DATA in a field (default `items`): {items: [DATA, ...]}.
- [Data Grid](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/datagrid.md) (`datagrid`): A table typed into the component: for each incoming envelope (usually the Start's only one) yields one envelope per row, the columns written into DATA (Override: only the columns).
- [Distinct](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/distinct.md) (`distinct`): Lets through (out-0) only the first envelope of each key and sends the repeated ones to the duplicates output (out-1, may stay unconnected).
- [Filter](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/filter.md) (`filter`): Evaluates a condition (an expression) on each envelope and sends it, unchanged, to the true output (out-0) or the false one (out-1, may stay unconnected: dropped).
- [Limit](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/limit.md) (`limit`): Lets only N envelopes through, unchanged: the first N as they arrive (top) or the last N when the input ends (bottom).
- [Lookup](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/lookup.md) (`lookup`): For each envelope of the input (in-0), finds the envelope of the lookup input (in-1) with the same key and writes its whole DATA into the output key (default `lookup`; null when not found, or a not found output).
- [Mapper](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/mapper.md) (`mapper`): Writes fields into the envelope's DATA: each field is a value (fixed or an expression on the incoming envelope) and the key it goes to; a key that exists is replaced.
- [Router](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/router.md) (`router`): Sends each envelope, unchanged, to the output of the first case whose condition is true (one output per case, in order), or to the last output, else (may stay unconnected: dropped).
- [Sort](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/sort.md) (`sort`): Reads every envelope, sorts them by a list of keys (an expression and ascending/descending; the next keys break ties, stable) and only then yields them.
- [Split](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/split.md) (`split`): The opposite of Aggregate: evaluates an expression that gives a list (default `$items`) and yields one envelope per item, the item as the whole DATA.
- [Break](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/break.md) (`break`): Only inside a Loop (`loop: <its id>`): an envelope that reaches it ends the loop after the iteration (it does not go out of the Loop), and wins over a Continue with or a Next reached in the same iteration.
- [Continue with](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/continue.md) (`continue`): Only inside a Loop (`loop: <its id>`): the envelope that reaches it is the loop state of the next iteration.
- [Discard](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/discard.md) (`discard`): The end of a path that leads nowhere on purpose: drops every envelope that reaches it (no output) and logs how many.
- [Flow Invoker](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/flow.md) (`flow`): Runs another flow of the project for each envelope, passing its Start's parameters and, with Send an input, the envelope's DATA or an expression as its input.
- [Log](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/log.md) (`log`): Evaluates a message (an expression on the envelope) and records it in the run's log of the component; the envelope goes on unchanged.
- [Loop](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/loop.md) (`loop`): Runs its loop region (nodes with `loop: <its id>`) again and again; each input envelope runs a loop of its own, in arrival order (parallel: 10 at once).
- [Next](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/next.md) (`next`): Only inside a Loop (`loop: <its id>`): an envelope that reaches it ends the iteration right away (what is still running in it stops; what reached Iteration end already went out) and the next one starts, with the loop state as it is (a Continue with reached before it still sets it).
- [Wait](https://github.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/blob/main/docs/components/wait.md) (`wait`): Holds the envelopes of `hold` until `watch` ends (everything before it finished), then lets each go on with {status: success | failure | empty, envelopes, errors, firstError, last} in its output key (default `wait`).

---

# The flow file

A flow is a YAML (or the same object as JSON) document, version 1: what the editor downloads and uploads, what the server keeps as a draft and what an agent reads and writes through the MCP.

## Shape

```yaml
version: 1 (the file format)
name: 'the flow name (the flow row keeps its own name: this one is informative)'
nodes:
    - id: unique in the flow; the Start is `start` and the End is `end` by convention
      type: a component type, or `start` / `end`
      label: 'optional: its name on the canvas and in the run record (default: the component name)'
      position: '{x, y} on the canvas (required; ~300 px apart left to right reads well)'
      config: the component's settings (see each component)
      outputKey: 'optional: the DATA key where it writes its result, for a component with a defaultOutputKey'
      override: 'optional, true: what it produces replaces DATA (only components with usesOverride)'
      disabled: 'optional, true: envelopes pass through it untouched'
      pinned: 'optional: {port: [DATA, ...]} replayed by test runs instead of running it'
      notes: 'optional: free text for people'
      loop: 'optional: the id of the Loop whose loop region holds this node directly (never on the Start or the End)'
      size: "a Loop's, {width, height}: where its Loop end card is on the canvas, as an offset from the Loop card's position"
edges:
    - source: node id
      sourcePort: out-N or error
      target: node id
      targetPort: in-N
groups:
    - id: string
      title: string
      color: string
      position: '{x, y}'
      size: '{width, height}'
```

## Ports

Inputs are in-0, in-1... and outputs out-0, out-1... in the order the component lists them. The error port is `error`, there only while the component's onError is divert. The Start has only out-0 and the End only in-0. A Loop has in-0 and out-0 (one edge each) facing outside, and two inner ports used from inside its loop region: `iteration-start` (a source, where each iteration starts) and `iteration-end` (a target, where the paths of an iteration finish), several edges each.

## The Start

Where every flow begins (not deletable, only an output). Its config holds whether the flow accepts an input (a webhook body, a calling flow's envelope, a test run's input), the input a test run uses by default, its type (a project script's type, `path#Name`) and the flow's parameters ($PARAMETERS). Without an input it yields one empty envelope; an input object is one envelope, a list one per item.

| Key                     | Label                | Kind        | Required | Default  | Notes                                                    |
| ----------------------- | -------------------- | ----------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `acceptsInput`          | Accepts input        | boolean     |          |          |                                                          |
| `inputType`             | Input type           | script-type |          |          | only when acceptsInput is `true`                         |
| `testInput`             | Default input (JSON) | code        |          |          | json; only when acceptsInput is `true`; e.g. `{"id": 1}` |
| `parameters`            | Parameters           | list        |          |          |                                                          |
| `parameters[].name`     | Name                 | text        | yes      |          | e.g. `since`                                             |
| `parameters[].type`     | Type                 | select      |          | `"text"` | one of `text`, `number`, `boolean`                       |
| `parameters[].default`  | Default              | text        |          |          |                                                          |
| `parameters[].required` | Required             | boolean     |          |          |                                                          |

## The End

Where every chain ends (only an input, several edges allowed). What reaches it is the flow's result: a calling Flow Invoker (wait) gets these envelopes.

## On error

Settings every component has, besides its own.

| Key       | Label    | Kind   | Required | Default   | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | -------- | ------ | -------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onError` | On error | select |          | `"throw"` | What an envelope that fails in the component does: throw stops the run; continue goes on as it came in; divert goes out through the error port (`error`), with DATA.errors.; one of `throw`, `continue`, `divert` |

## Connections

A component that talks to a database or an API picks a connection profile of the workspace by its id in config.connection (list_connections gives them), or leaves it '' and fills the profile's fields in its own config (password-like fields always name a secret of the workspace). Any of them may set config.connection = '$dynamic' and name the profile in config.connectionName: a text, or an expression on $PARAMETERS, $VARIABLES and $SECRETS only (never the envelope: $DATA or its keys), evaluated once, so the component uses one connection for the whole run (e.g. "'Orders_' + $PARAMETERS.env"). To use another connection per item, a Flow Invoker calls a flow with the name as a parameter.

## Calling by expression

A Flow Invoker's flowId (or a Script Invoker's function) set to '$dynamic' takes the flow (function) from an expression on each envelope (flowPath / functionPath).

## Expressions

JavaScript expressions evaluated on each envelope (no statements, no `return`). Keep each one short: a value, a condition, a small formula. Logic with helpers, several statements or validation (an IIFE such as `(() => { ... })()`) reads better in a TypeScript component, which can import project scripts, or a Script Invoker; validate_flow warns about it (a suggestion, not an error).

- $<key>: a top-level key of the envelope DATA ($price, $customer.name, $items[0])
- $DATA: the whole DATA object
- $PARAMETERS.<name>: the Start parameters of the run
- $VARIABLES.<name>: the workspace's variables
- $SECRETS.<name> / $SECRETS['name']: the workspace's secret values (masked in the logs)
- $FLOW_CURRENT_RUN: the run, the same in every envelope: {id, mode, workspace, project, flow, startedAt, parentId?}
- $_loopIndex: in a Loop's loop region and its stop condition, the number of the iteration, 0 in the first; in nested Loops, that of the Loop whose region holds the component directly

### $FLOW_CURRENT_RUN

- `id`: the run's id (a flow a Flow Invoker calls runs as a run of its own, with its own id)
- `mode`: `validation` in a test run (the editor's Run, test_run: nothing is written outside), `execution` in a run for real (Run for real, a schedule, a webhook)
- `workspace`: the workspace's name
- `project`: the project's name
- `flow`: the flow's name, not its id (e.g. for a log or an error message: `$FLOW_CURRENT_RUN.flow`)
- `startedAt`: when the run started, ISO 8601 in UTC (e.g. 2026-11-09T00:45:54.260Z)
- `parentId`: only in a flow called by a Flow Invoker: the id of the run that called it

A setting of kind `value` is {value, expression}: expression false = the text as it is; true = an expression. In a list item marked `spread`, value and expression are the item's own keys ({name, value, expression}).

Output keys and field names: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit, and not FLOW_CURRENT_RUN, PARAMETERS, SECRETS, VARIABLES, DATA.

## Rules

What `validate_flow` (and every run) checks:

- The file has version 1, a name, and nodes each with an id (unique), a type and a position.
- Exactly one Start and one End.
- Every edge connects two nodes of the flow, on ports their components have with their config (an edge on a port that is gone is an error).
- Every port takes several edges (an output copies each envelope to all of them; an input joins them in arrival order), except the Lookup: one edge on each of its inputs.
- The same two ports are not connected twice, and the Start never goes straight to the End.
- Edges out of the error port (`error`) only from a component whose onError is divert.
- No cycles: the flow is a directed acyclic graph (a Loop's iteration-start → … → iteration-end is a path inside its region, not a cycle).
- A loop region is closed: an edge joins two nodes with the same `loop` (a Loop's inner ports count as inside its region, its in-0 and out-0 as outside). The Start and End have no `loop`; a Continue with, a Next and a Break always have one; a `loop` names a Loop of the flow. Loops nest (a Loop with a `loop` is inside another), but never inside themselves, directly or through others.
- Every component type exists; each enabled component passes its own checks (required settings, names, SQL read only, and so on).
- Expressions compile (syntax only; unknown $variables are not an error, a key may come from upstream).
- Output keys and field names are valid names (letters, digits, _; not a reserved name).
- A Flow Invoker calls a flow of the same project; scripts are the project's. Connection profiles and secrets are the workspace's: one it does not have yet (by id, or a dynamic connection name known before the run) is a warning, not an issue: the draft is saved, and the run fails at that component until a person creates it.
- The Start's parameters have unique valid names and defaults of their type; its default input is valid JSON.
- Pinned outputs take at most 2 MB in all.

## Patterns

Ways to combine the components for common needs. Read them before designing a flow that does one of these.

### Do something once, after everything before it finished, knowing how it ended (a barrier)

A step must happen once and only after all the envelopes of a process were handled: advance a checkpoint, release a lock, report a failure, log a total. Also when nothing may come out of that process (an empty source).

- Use a Wait. Its `hold` input takes the envelope that goes on afterwards (e.g. the one that took the lock, with its ids); its `watch` input takes what comes out of the process: its output AND its error port (onError `divert`), both edges into `watch`.
- When `watch` ends (every component before it finished with every envelope) the held envelope goes on once with `$wait` = {status, envelopes, errors, firstError, last}: status `success` (envelopes arrived, no errors), `failure` (an envelope came from an error port) or `empty` (nothing arrived). It always answers, even when the process produced nothing.
- After it, a Router on `$wait.status`: success → advance the checkpoint; empty → release only (or advance, when an empty window is complete for you); failure → release, then a component that throws `$wait.firstError.message` so the run ends as failed.
- Without a status, a Limit with mode `bottom` (Last) and count 1 is the simplest barrier: it lets the last envelope through when its input ends, and nothing when no envelope arrives. With a Limit, keep onError `throw` on the components before it: an envelope that failed with `continue` or `divert` does not stop the run, so the barrier would still open.

### Incremental load with a checkpoint (watermark)

Each run reads only what changed since the last run that finished, from a source with a change date or an increasing key.

- Keep the checkpoint in a control table (one row per source: name, checkpoint). The run reads it first (a SQL Server or Redshift query) and computes the window end (`to`, e.g. now) once; the window is checkpoint → to. When the process calls another flow per source, pass the window as parameters.
- Read the window (a Pipeline or query with checkpoint < date <= to), process and write.
- Then a Wait (the barrier pattern): `hold` = the envelope with the source and the window, `watch` = the output and the error port of the processing. On success, a SQL Server Update of the control row: set checkpoint = `to`, Match on the source name, Expected values checkpoint = the old one (compare-and-set) and If no row matches = Error, so a concurrent run that moved it first is an error, not a silent overwrite.
- An empty window is safe either way: keeping the checkpoint, the next run reads from the same point up to its own `to`, covering it again. A failed run does not move it: the next run reads that window again, so the writes must be idempotent (an upsert or an update by key, not a plain insert).
- A Flow Invoker that waits passes on the envelopes that reach the End of the called flow as they arrive, and none when nothing reaches it: it is not a "finished" signal by itself. Its output and its error port into the `watch` of a Wait are: the Wait answers when the call finished, with how.

### One run at a time (a lock)

Two runs must not process the same source at once (a schedule that overlaps a slow run).

- A lock row in the control table (name, lockedBy, lockedUntil). At the start, read it; when it is free (lockedBy null) or expired (lockedUntil in the past), take it with a SQL Server Update: set lockedBy = the run, lockedUntil = now + a timeout, Expected values = the lockedBy and lockedUntil just read (compare-and-set) and If no row matches = Error. Two runs that read the same free lock: only one Update matches.
- At the end, after a Wait (the barrier pattern), release it whatever the status: set lockedBy and lockedUntil to null, Expected values lockedBy = the run.
- A run that is cancelled or whose worker stops does not release it: the expiry (lockedUntil) frees it for the next run. Choose a timeout longer than the slowest run.

## Example

```yaml
version: 1
name: Active customers to the CRM
nodes:
    - id: start
      type: start
      position: { x: 0, y: 0 }
      config:
          parameters:
              - { name: since, type: text, default: '2026-01-01' }
    - id: read
      type: sqlserver
      label: Read customers
      position: { x: 300, y: 0 }
      config:
          connection: <connection profile id>
          sql: |
              SELECT id, name, email FROM Customer WHERE updatedAt > @since
          parameters:
              - { name: since, value: $PARAMETERS.since, expression: true }
    - id: active
      type: filter
      position: { x: 600, y: 0 }
      config:
          condition: $email != null
    - id: send
      type: http-request
      position: { x: 900, y: 0 }
      config:
          connection: <connection profile id>
          method: POST
          url: { value: 'https://crm.example.com/contacts', expression: false }
          body: { value: '{name: $name, email: $email}', expression: true }
          onError: divert
    - id: failed
      type: log
      position: { x: 1200, y: 200 }
      config:
          level: warn
          message: '`could not send ${$id}: ${$errors[0].message}`'
    - id: end
      type: end
      position: { x: 1200, y: 0 }
      config: {}
edges:
    - { source: start, sourcePort: out-0, target: read, targetPort: in-0 }
    - { source: read, sourcePort: out-0, target: active, targetPort: in-0 }
    - { source: active, sourcePort: out-0, target: send, targetPort: in-0 }
    - { source: send, sourcePort: out-0, target: end, targetPort: in-0 }
    - { source: send, sourcePort: error, target: failed, targetPort: in-0 }
    - { source: failed, sourcePort: out-0, target: end, targetPort: in-0 }
```

## In a git repository

A workspace mirrored to git is a folder of its own on the environment's branch, in a public format (version 1) that the app, a person or another tool can write. The name of a project, folder, flow, connection or script is its path; its identity (`id`, a UUID in lower case) is in its file, so a rename or a move is a move of the file. Every name is a valid file name everywhere (no `\ / : * ? " < > |`, no name Windows reserves, at most 64 characters, unique among its siblings whatever the case) and a path in the repository has at most 150 characters, so a clone on Windows works.

```text
.gitattributes                         # * text=auto eol=lf, written on the first export
<workspace>/
  workspace.yaml                       # format: 1
  connections/<connection name>.yaml   # id, type
  projects/<project name>/
    project.yaml                       # id, description, icon, color
    flows/<folder>/<flow name>.flow.yaml
    scripts/<script path>.ts
```

An empty folder of flows or of scripts keeps a `.gitkeep`. A file anywhere else is not part of the format.

### workspace.yaml

`format: 1`, the version of the format. A change to the format gets a new number.

### A connection

`connections/<connection name>.yaml` declares a connection: its `id` and its `type` only. Its configuration and credentials stay on each server, so no secret reaches git; a connection that arrives on a server from git is not configured there until someone configures it. Secrets and variables are not in the repository: a flow names them only.

```yaml
id: 0b6f3c1e-2a7d-4f0e-9c4b-5d8e1a2f3b4c
type: sqlserver
```

### project.yaml

The project's `id`, and its `description`, `icon` and `color`, each optional.

### A flow

`flows/<folder>/<flow name>.flow.yaml` is the flow file described above, with three differences: it has the flow's `id` (required); it has no `name`, which is the file name without `.flow.yaml`; it has no `pinned` outputs, which are test data and stay on the server. It may say `deployed: false` when the flow is not deployed; absent means `true`. A flow names the connections and the flows it calls by id, and scripts by path.

The server writes a flow once it has been deployed: the deployed version, or, after an undeploy, the version deployed last with `deployed: false`. A draft never reaches the repository, and an archived flow, folder or project leaves it.

### A script

`scripts/<script path>.ts`: the project's script, as it is. A script is identified by its path.

### The stable order

Every file the app writes is in one canonical order: a flow's nodes by id, its edges by source, target and then ports, its groups by id, and every key of a node's `config` from a to z (at every depth; lists keep their order). So writing a file the app read gives no diff, and two branches that each add a node rarely conflict. The app reads any order and any YAML formatting (flow style, quotes, CRLF line endings).

Comments are not part of the format: the app drops them when it writes a file. What a comment would say goes in a node's `notes`.

### Versions

A deploy makes a new version only when what the engine runs changed. A version's content hash leaves out `deployed`, the name, the canvas (positions, groups, notes), the pinned outputs, the order of nodes, edges and keys, and line endings (LF or CRLF): changing only `deployed` makes no new version.

### Validation of a tree

The app checks a whole workspace tree before applying it (`validateWorkspaceTree` in the core). An error refuses the tree whole, with the reasons listed: a file that is not valid YAML or does not match its schema (an unknown key included); an `id` missing, not a UUID in lower case, or in two files of a kind; a `workspace.yaml` or a `project.yaml` missing; an edge to a node that does not exist; a call to a flow that is not in the workspace or to a script that is not in the project; a connection a flow uses and the workspace does not declare; a name breaking the rule above or a path too long; two names that differ only in case or Unicode normalization. A warning does not: a declared connection not configured on this server; a secret or variable a flow reads with no value on this server; a comment in a flow file; a repository without `.gitattributes`; a file that is not part of the format (it is left out).

### JSON Schemas

A JSON Schema for each file, for an editor to check the files as they are written:

| Schema                                                     | Files                        | For        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------- |
| [`flow.schema.json`](schemas/flow.schema.json)             | `**/*.flow.yaml`             | flow       |
| [`project.schema.json`](schemas/project.schema.json)       | `**/projects/*/project.yaml` | project    |
| [`connection.schema.json`](schemas/connection.schema.json) | `**/connections/*.yaml`      | connection |
| [`workspace.schema.json`](schemas/workspace.schema.json)   | `**/workspace.yaml`          | workspace  |

In VS Code, with the YAML extension, in the settings:

```json
{
    "yaml.schemas": {
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/main/docs/schemas/flow.schema.json": ["**/*.flow.yaml"],
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/main/docs/schemas/project.schema.json": ["**/projects/*/project.yaml"],
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/main/docs/schemas/connection.schema.json": ["**/connections/*.yaml"],
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flowtinus-hub/flowtinus/main/docs/schemas/workspace.schema.json": ["**/workspace.yaml"]
    }
}
```

---

# Connection types

A connection profile is a reusable way into a system (a database, an API), kept in a workspace for all its projects. A flow refers to it by id; a sensitive field never holds a value, it names one of the secrets of the workspace. Profiles and secrets are created in the editor (the Connections and the Secrets and Variables pages of the workspace).

## APIs

### REST Basic Authentication (`rest-basic`)

A REST API with HTTP Basic authentication (user and password). Used by the HTTP Request component.

| Field      | Label                                        | Kind     | Required | Default | Notes                                                               |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `user`     | Username                                     | text     | yes      |         |                                                                     |
| `password` | Password                                     | secret   | yes      |         | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile) |
| `headers`  | Default headers (one "Name: value" per line) | textarea |          |         |                                                                     |

### REST OAuth 2.0 (`rest-oauth2`)

A REST API with OAuth 2.0 client credentials: the token is fetched and cached by the runner. Used by the HTTP Request component.

| Field          | Label                    | Kind   | Required | Default             | Notes                                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grant`        | Grant type               | select | yes      | `clientCredentials` | one of `clientCredentials`                                          |
| `authorizeUrl` | Authorization URL        | text   | yes      |                     | only when grant is `authorizationCode`                              |
| `tokenUrl`     | Token URL                | text   | yes      |                     |                                                                     |
| `clientId`     | Client ID                | text   | yes      |                     |                                                                     |
| `clientSecret` | Client secret            | secret | yes      |                     | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile) |
| `scopes`       | Scopes (space separated) | text   |          |                     |                                                                     |
| `audience`     | Audience                 | text   |          |                     |                                                                     |

### HTTP Client Account (`http-client`)

Any HTTP API: no authentication, a bearer token or an API key header, plus default headers. Used by the HTTP Request component.

| Field          | Label                                        | Kind     | Required | Default     | Notes                                                                                           |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auth`         | Authentication                               | select   | yes      | `none`      | one of `none`, `bearer`, `apiKey`                                                               |
| `token`        | Token                                        | secret   | yes      |             | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile); only when auth is `bearer` |
| `apiKeyHeader` | Header name                                  | text     | yes      | `X-API-Key` | only when auth is `apiKey`                                                                      |
| `apiKey`       | API key                                      | secret   | yes      |             | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile); only when auth is `apiKey` |
| `headers`      | Default headers (one "Name: value" per line) | textarea |          |             |                                                                                                 |
| `timeout`      | Timeout (seconds)                            | number   |          | `30`        |                                                                                                 |

A component may fill `auth`, `token`, `apiKeyHeader`, `apiKey` in its own config instead of picking a profile.

### SOAP (`soap`)

A SOAP service (basic or WS-Security authentication). No component uses it yet.

| Field      | Label          | Kind   | Required | Default | Notes                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | -------------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auth`     | Authentication | select | yes      | `none`  | one of `none`, `basic`, `wsSecurity`                                                                           |
| `user`     | Username       | text   | yes      |         | only when auth is `basic` or `wsSecurity`                                                                      |
| `password` | Password       | secret | yes      |         | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile); only when auth is `basic` or `wsSecurity` |

### Azure Blob Storage (`azure-blob`)

| Field              | Label             | Kind   | Required | Default            | Notes                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `connectionString` | Connection string | secret | yes      |                    | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile); only when auth is `connectionString` |

### Google Cloud Storage (`gcs`)

| `user`       | User                    | text   | yes      |         |                                                                     |

| `directory`  | Directory               | text   |          | `/`     |                                                                     |

A MongoDB database (a connection string kept as a secret). Used by the MongoDB Pipeline, Upsert and Delete components.

| Field              | Label             | Kind   | Required | Default | Notes                                                               |

A component may fill `connectionString` in its own config instead of picking a profile.

### Amazon Redshift (`redshift`)

An Amazon Redshift database. Used by the Redshift components (Query, Insert, Upsert, Delete, Execute). Its Test connection says which server it reaches (kept with the profile): one that answers as PostgreSQL gets a warning, since SQL written for one may not run on the other.

| Field      | Label    | Kind   | Required | Default | Notes                                                               |
| ---------- | -------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`     | Host     | text   | yes      |         |                                                                     |
| `port`     | Port     | number | yes      | `5439`  |                                                                     |
| `database` | Database | text   | yes      |         |                                                                     |
| `user`     | User     | text   | yes      |         |                                                                     |
| `password` | Password | secret | yes      |         | names a secret of the workspace (the value is never in the profile) |
| `ssl`      | SSL      | select | yes      | `on`    | one of `on`, `off`                                                  |

A component may fill `host`, `port`, `database`, `user`, `password`, `ssl` in its own config instead of picking a profile.

# MongoDB Delete

For each envelope, deletes every document of the collection (database and collection fixed or expressions on the envelope) that matches the filter (an expression on the envelope, as in mongosh) and the envelope goes on with {deleted} in its output key (default `mongodb`). An empty filter is refused unless Delete all is on. A test run only counts what would be deleted.

- Type: `mongodb-delete` (Databases)
- Inputs: `in-0`
- Outputs: `out-0`
- Error port: `error` while `onError` is `divert`
- Output key: `mongodb` by default (the node's `outputKey` changes it)
- Override: yes (the node's `override: true` makes what it produces the whole DATA)
- Writes outside the run: yes (a test run does not write)

## Settings

| Key                | Label                                                     | Kind       | Required | Default                           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connection`       | Connection                                                | connection |          |                                   | profile type `mongodb`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `connectionName`   | Connection name                                           | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":true}`  | The name of a connection of the workspace, from $PARAMETERS, $VARIABLES and $SECRETS only: the same for every envelope. To use another connection per item, call a flow (Flow Invoker) with the name as a parameter.; only when connection is `"$dynamic"`; e.g. `'Orders_' + $PARAMETERS.env` |
| `connectionString` | Connection string                                         | secret     | yes      |                                   | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `database`         | Database                                                  | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":false}` | e.g. `From the connection`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `collection`       | Collection                                                | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":false}` | e.g. `orders`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `filter`           | Filter                                                    | code       | yes      | `"{\n  field: $field\n}"`         | javascript                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `allowAll`         | Delete all (an empty filter deletes the whole collection) | boolean    |          |                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Every component also has `onError` (see [the flow format](../flow-format.md#on-error)).

## Example config

```yaml
connection: <connection profile id>
collection:
    value: sessions
    expression: false
filter: '{ customerId: $id }'
```

---

# MongoDB Pipeline

Runs an aggregation pipeline (written as in Compass or mongosh, an expression on the incoming envelope: `{$match: {cpf: $cpf}}`) on a collection (database and collection fixed or expressions on the envelope) once per incoming envelope and yields one envelope per document, the fields written into DATA. Read only: $out and $merge are refused. Output is plain JSON by default; canonical Extended JSON preserves BSON types for a MongoDB Upsert configured with the same format, and rejects documents that cannot be represented losslessly.

- Type: `mongodb-pipeline` (Databases)
- Inputs: `in-0`
- Outputs: `out-0`
- Error port: `error` while `onError` is `divert`
- Output key: none (writes into DATA)
- Override: yes (the node's `override: true` makes what it produces the whole DATA)
- Writes outside the run: no

## Settings

| Key                | Label             | Kind       | Required | Default                                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connection`       | Connection        | connection |          |                                                                | profile type `mongodb`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `connectionName`   | Connection name   | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":true}`                               | The name of a connection of the workspace, from $PARAMETERS, $VARIABLES and $SECRETS only: the same for every envelope. To use another connection per item, call a flow (Flow Invoker) with the name as a parameter.; only when connection is `"$dynamic"`; e.g. `'Orders_' + $PARAMETERS.env` |
| `connectionString` | Connection string | secret     | yes      |                                                                | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `database`         | Database          | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":false}`                              | e.g. `From the connection`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `collection`       | Collection        | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":false}`                              | e.g. `orders`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pipeline`         | Pipeline          | code       | yes      | `"[\n  {\n    $match: {}\n  },\n  {\n    $limit: 100\n  }\n]"` | javascript                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `outputFormat`     | Output format     | select     |          | `"plain"`                                                      | one of `plain`, `extended-json`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `timeoutS`         | Timeout (seconds) | number     |          | `300`                                                          | 1 to …                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Every component also has `onError` (see [the flow format](../flow-format.md#on-error)).

## Example config

```yaml
connection: <connection profile id>
collection:
    value: orders
    expression: false
pipeline: |-
    [
      { $match: { status: 'open' } },
      { $limit: 100 },
    ]
timeoutS: 60
```

---

# MongoDB Upsert

Writes each envelope into a collection (database and collection fixed or expressions on the envelope; batches kept per collection): updates ($set) or replaces the document matching the filter, or inserts it. The document is the whole DATA or an expression; `_id` is taken from the filter when inserting. Writes in batches; each envelope goes on with {matched, upsertedId} in its output key (default `mongodb`). A test run writes nothing. Select canonical Extended JSON when the filter and document contain BSON values in that format; reserved Extended JSON forms are interpreted as BSON values.

- Type: `mongodb-upsert` (Databases)
- Inputs: `in-0`
- Outputs: `out-0`
- Error port: `error` while `onError` is `divert`
- Output key: `mongodb` by default (the node's `outputKey` changes it)
- Override: yes (the node's `override: true` makes what it produces the whole DATA)
- Writes outside the run: yes (a test run does not write)

## Settings

| Key                | Label                   | Kind       | Required | Default                           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ---------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connection`       | Connection              | connection |          |                                   | profile type `mongodb`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `connectionName`   | Connection name         | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":true}`  | The name of a connection of the workspace, from $PARAMETERS, $VARIABLES and $SECRETS only: the same for every envelope. To use another connection per item, call a flow (Flow Invoker) with the name as a parameter.; only when connection is `"$dynamic"`; e.g. `'Orders_' + $PARAMETERS.env` |
| `connectionString` | Connection string       | secret     | yes      |                                   | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `database`         | Database                | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":false}` | e.g. `From the connection`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `collection`       | Collection              | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":false}` | e.g. `orders`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `filter`           | Match on                | list       | yes      |                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `filter[].field`   | Field                   | text       | yes      |                                   | e.g. `email`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `filter[].value`   | Value                   | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":true}`  | stored as the item's own `value` and `expression`; e.g. `$email`                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `source`           | Document                | select     |          | `"data"`                          | one of `data`, `expression`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `document`         | Expression              | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":true}`  | only when source is `"expression"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `valueFormat`      | Value format            | select     |          | `"plain"`                         | one of `plain`, `extended-json`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `writeMode`        | When a document matches | select     |          | `"update"`                        | one of `update`, `replace`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `batchSize`        | Batch size              | number     |          | `500`                             | 1 to 10000                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Every component also has `onError` (see [the flow format](../flow-format.md#on-error)).

## Example config

```yaml
connection: <connection profile id>
collection:
    value: customers
    expression: false
filter:
    - field: email
      value: $email
      expression: true
source: data
batchSize: 100
```

---

# Redshift Delete

Deletes the rows of an Amazon Redshift table whose Match on columns all equal the envelope's values (each a value or an expression on the envelope; null or undefined is an error for that envelope, never a wider delete). Rows go in batches of one table, each in one transaction (all or none of that batch): one DELETE per batch. Each envelope goes on with {action: "deleted", rows} or {action: "notFound"} in its output key (default `redshift`). A test run deletes nothing.

- Type: `redshift-delete` (Databases)
- Inputs: `in-0`
- Outputs: `out-0`
- Error port: `error` while `onError` is `divert`
- Output key: `redshift` by default (the node's `outputKey` changes it)
- Override: yes (the node's `override: true` makes what it produces the whole DATA)
- Writes outside the run: yes (a test run does not write)

## Settings

| Key                | Label             | Kind       | Required | Default                           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ---------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connection`       | Connection        | connection |          |                                   | profile type `redshift`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `connectionName`   | Connection name   | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":true}`  | The name of a connection of the workspace, from $PARAMETERS, $VARIABLES and $SECRETS only: the same for every envelope. To use another connection per item, call a flow (Flow Invoker) with the name as a parameter.; only when connection is `"$dynamic"`; e.g. `'Orders_' + $PARAMETERS.env`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `host`             | Host              | text       | yes      |                                   | only when connection is `""`; e.g. `db.example.com`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `port`             | Port              | number     | yes      | `"5439"`                          | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `database`         | Database          | text       | yes      |                                   | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `user`             | User              | text       | yes      |                                   | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `password`         | Password          | secret     | yes      |                                   | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ssl`              | SSL               | select     | yes      | `"on"`                            | one of `on`, `off`; only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `table`            | Table             | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":false}` | schema.table or table; with fx, an expression on the envelope (e.g. $tenant + ".customers"), its result checked the same way. A batch is one table: an envelope whose table is another closes the batch (envelopes sorted by table, e.g. a Sort before it, make full batches instead of small ones), and each batch is atomic on its own (all or none of that batch, never of the run). The last log line says what happened per table.; e.g. `sales.customers` |
| `columns`          | Match on          | list       | yes      |                                   | The rows deleted are those whose columns all equal these values (WHERE column = value AND ...). A value that is null or undefined is an error for that envelope: nothing is deleted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `columns[].column` | Column            | text       | yes      |                                   | e.g. `email`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `columns[].value`  | Value             | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":true}`  | stored as the item's own `value` and `expression`; e.g. `$email`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ifNotFound`       | If no row matches | select     |          | `"continue"`                      | Continue: the envelope goes on with {action: "notFound"}. Error: it goes to the On error policy.; one of `continue`, `error`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `batchSize`        | Batch size        | number     |          | `500`                             | The most rows per batch (one transaction); an envelope of another table closes the batch before that.; 1 to 5000                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `timeoutS`         | Timeout (seconds) | number     |          | `300`                             | 1 to …                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Every component also has `onError` (see [the flow format](../flow-format.md#on-error)).

## Example config

```yaml
connection: <connection profile id>
table: sales.order_events
columns:
    - column: order_id
      value: $id
      expression: true
batchSize: 500
```

---

# Redshift Execute

Runs any SQL on Amazon Redshift (one or more statements; nothing checks what it does) once per envelope, in a transaction of its own: a COMMIT or ROLLBACK in the SQL is its own; what is still open at the end is committed (At the end: Commit, the default) or rolled back; an error rolls back. The `@name`s are parameters (a value or an expression on the envelope); a `{{name}}` is a schema or table name picked in the run (checked, then pasted) (or a list of names: a, b, c). The envelope goes on with {rowsAffected, rows, transaction} in its output key (default `redshift`). A test run runs nothing.

- Type: `redshift-execute` (Databases)
- Inputs: `in-0`
- Outputs: `out-0`
- Error port: `error` while `onError` is `divert`
- Output key: `redshift` by default (the node's `outputKey` changes it)
- Override: yes (the node's `override: true` makes what it produces the whole DATA)
- Writes outside the run: yes (a test run does not write)

## Settings

| Key                  | Label             | Kind       | Required | Default                          | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connection`         | Connection        | connection |          |                                  | profile type `redshift`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `connectionName`     | Connection name   | value      | yes      | `{"value":"","expression":true}` | The name of a connection of the workspace, from $PARAMETERS, $VARIABLES and $SECRETS only: the same for every envelope. To use another connection per item, call a flow (Flow Invoker) with the name as a parameter.; only when connection is `"$dynamic"`; e.g. `'Orders_' + $PARAMETERS.env` |
| `host`               | Host              | text       | yes      |                                  | only when connection is `""`; e.g. `db.example.com`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `port`               | Port              | number     | yes      | `"5439"`                         | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `database`           | Database          | text       | yes      |                                  | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `user`               | User              | text       | yes      |                                  | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `password`           | Password          | secret     | yes      |                                  | only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ssl`                | SSL               | select     | yes      | `"on"`                           | one of `on`, `off`; only when connection is `""`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `sql`                | SQL               | code       | yes      |                                  | Any SQL, one or more statements, run as written in one transaction (a COMMIT or ROLLBACK in it is its own). Nothing checks what it does.; sql; e.g. `UPDATE sales.orders SET status = @status WHERE id = @id`                                                                                  |
| `parameters`         | Parameters        | list       |          |                                  | Each @name the SQL uses, with its value (sent as a parameter); a {{name}} in the SQL (e.g. {{schema}}.briefs) is pasted as a name, after it is checked; a list of names (e.g. ["id", "name"]) is pasted as id, name, each item one simple name (no schema.name), an empty list an error.       |
| `parameters[].name`  | Name              | text       | yes      |                                  | e.g. `id`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `parameters[].value` | Value             | value      |          | `{"value":"","expression":true}` | stored as the item's own `value` and `expression`; e.g. `$id`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `atEnd`              | At the end        | select     |          | `"commit"`                       | What happens to the transaction still open when the SQL ends without error: Commit, or Rollback (only what the SQL committed itself stays). An error always rolls back.; one of `commit`, `rollback`                                                                                           |
| `timeoutS`           | Timeout (seconds) | number     |          | `300`                            | 1 to …                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Every component also has `onError` (see [the flow format](../flow-format.md#on-error)).

## Example config

```yaml
connection: <connection profile id>
sql: |-
    DELETE FROM {{schema}}.projects WHERE brief_id = @briefId;
    INSERT INTO {{schema}}.projects (brief_id, name) VALUES (@briefId, @name);
parameters:
    - name: schema
      value: $tenant
      expression: true
    - name: briefId
      value: $id
      expression: true
    - name: name
      value: $project.name
      expression: true
atEnd: commit
```
